name: Maximiliano (Max) Sanchez
headline: Economics student at Florida State University
pitch: I'm interested in behavioral economics, AI and human decision-making, and fintech. Most of what I build sits where economics meets data: how people make choices, and how tools, including AI, change those choices.
about: I'm from Cali, Colombia, and I've lived and worked in Mexico, Panama and Italy. I'm an economics major with a psychology minor at Florida State University. I'm finishing my first two years at FSU's Panama campus and move to Tallahassee in Fall 2027, with graduation projected for May 2029.
My research usually starts from a claim that's spreading online. I trace it back to the papers and data, write up what holds and what doesn't, and build a small model so anyone can test the idea.
Outside of work I'm happiest traveling, getting to know new cultures, playing sports and being outdoors.

sections.title: Research
sections.intro: Case studies that start from a popular claim and end with evidence and a working model.

projects.title: The free massage upsell
projects.summary: Why who "free" attracts matters more than any sales script.
projects.detail: A viral reel told massage therapists to give away free sessions and pause halfway to sell the rest. Every piece of the tactic has real psychology behind it: zero price, reciprocity, a relaxed client, a good experience cut off in the middle. The weak spot is who free pulls in. In the model, choosing who gets the free session matters more than anything said on the table.
built: Reviewed 15 sources, from the zero-price effect to Groupon retention data
Built a 12-month funnel model comparing four pricing strategies
Adapted it to a dog-daycare business as a second case

projects.title: The world's #3 economy that speaks Spanish
projects.summary: A viral economic claim, checked against IMF data.
projects.detail: A Spanish-language reel claimed Hispanic America, counted as one country, would be the world's third-largest economy, served by fewer than 1,000 Spanish-speaking financial planners. The #3 claim holds up, even without U.S. Latinos, barely. The planner count depends entirely on how you define a planner.
built: Rebuilt the ranking from IMF 2026 data
Modeled the bloc with and without U.S. Latinos
Compared definitions of financial planner and advisor

projects.title: Mining organic hooks for paid ads
projects.summary: Do viral TikTok openings make good ads?
projects.detail: A popular tip says to search TikTok for your customer's problem and reuse the most-viewed openings in ads. It's a solid way to generate ideas, but views aren't sales. In bait-heavy niches, the most-viewed hooks can convert worse than random ones, and many can't legally run as ads.
built: Reviewed research on reach vs. persuasion and native ads
Wrote a hook-mining script that ranks by views relative to followers
Simulated the winner's curse in picking ads by views

projects.title: Farm-gate cold rooms in India
projects.summary: Unit economics of a pay-per-crate solar cold room.
projects.detail: India doesn't lack cold storage. It lacks the first mile: pre-cooling, packing and refrigerated trucks between farm and store. A shared solar cold room helps, but on storage fees alone it barely pays back. The opportunity is running it as the entry point to a chain.
built: Pinned the cold-chain gap on the first mile, not storage
Built a payback model for a pay-per-crate cold room
Laid out the business model around it

projects.title: Shirtsleeves to shirtsleeves
projects.summary: How family fortunes vanish, and how to plan under Colombian law.
projects.detail: Why the Vanderbilt fortune vanished, what the "Rockefeller Waterfall" structure really is, and how it could be adapted under Colombian law. Written in English and Spanish. Educational research, not financial or legal advice.
built: Compared the Vanderbilt and Rockefeller histories
Mapped the structure onto Colombian legal tools
Built a 150-year wealth simulation in Python

projects.title: The "buy Chinese stocks" thesis
projects.summary: A viral investing thesis, tested with real ETF data.
projects.detail: Tests a viral "buy Chinese stocks now" thesis by comparing China ETFs (MCHI, FXI, KWEB, ASHR) with the S&P 500, and explains how Latin American investors could access them. Educational research, not investment advice.
built: Pulled and compared ETF performance data
Weighed the thesis against the numbers
Compared access routes for LatAm investors

projects.title: Pairs trading research
projects.detail: A statistical pairs-trading analysis: testing whether two assets move together over the long run, tracking how far their spread drifts, and backtesting a strategy that trades on it. Research, not financial advice.
built: Ran cointegration tests on candidate pairs
Computed spread z-scores
Backtested the strategy

sections.title: Tools
sections.intro: Software I built to make research and writing faster, all open source.

projects.title: Reel → Repo
projects.summary: An AI agent that turns a link into a published case study.
projects.detail: Paste a reel link, article or one-line idea and type /research. A Claude Code skill watches the reel, fact-checks it, researches it, writes and runs code, draws diagrams and a cover, then publishes the result as its own GitHub repo. Most projects on this site started this way. No API keys, $0 per run.
built: Designed the end-to-end research workflow
Wrote checks for sources, links, voice and diagrams
Automated publishing to GitHub

projects.title: TapReview outreach CRM
projects.summary: A local CRM that runs my daily outreach for TapReview.
projects.detail: I built my own CRM to run TapReview's daily prospecting. It keeps every contact and follow-up in one SQLite database, drafts personalized messages with an LLM, and shows the day's batch on a local web dashboard. Sending stays manual: I review and send every message myself.
built: Designed the contact pipeline and follow-up logic
Connected an LLM API to draft personalized messages
Built a local web dashboard and a command-line version

projects.title: AEO copywriting skill
projects.summary: Write web pages that AI answer engines quote.
projects.detail: Fact-checks Ahrefs' popular answer engine optimization course against the studies behind it. Most stats hold up, but they're correlations and a few apply only to Google. The writing advice was the most useful part, so I turned it into a Claude skill plus a linter that scores copy section by section.
built: Traced 10+ statistics to their original studies
Wrote a Claude skill for AEO copy
Built a Python linter for answer-first, citable writing

projects.title: Humanizer
projects.summary: Strip AI-writing tells from a draft.
projects.detail: A Claude skill that edits AI-drafted text in three passes: find the tells, rewrite without them, report what changed. Research shows words like "delve" spiked after ChatGPT launched, but no list of tells can prove a text is AI. The goal is writing that reads well.
built: Reviewed research on AI word frequency
Wrote a three-pass editing skill
Built a detector for the same tells

projects.title: Video editing skill
projects.summary: Turn a raw talking-head video into a captioned short.
projects.detail: A viral reel claimed a downloadable Claude skill edits your videos. It can, but only by driving ffmpeg and Whisper, since Claude can't watch video. I built a working version that cuts dead air, captions in short chunks inside safe zones, and mixes in music.
built: Built silence detection and cutting with ffmpeg
Added Whisper transcription and timed captions
Placed captions outside the platform button zones
